 Community Outreach Strategies That Actually Work 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 May 7, 2025 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Outreach Strategies for Community-Based Organizations: 7 Tactics That Actually Work 



 Want to really connect with your community? Tired of outreach efforts that fall flat? Many organizations struggle to make a lasting impact. It’s a common problem. But what if there was a better way? What if you could build stronger connections and drive real change? 



 This guide gives you seven proven outreach tactics. We’ll show you how to go beyond basic outreach and build meaningful relationships. We will cover: 



 
 Building strong partnerships. 



 Leveraging social media effectively. 



 Hosting engaging community events. 



 Using local media outreach. 



 Implementing targeted email campaigns. 



 Creating valuable content. 



 Utilizing data-driven strategies. 
 



 A study by the Pew Research Center found that 72% of Americans use social media. We’ll show you how to use this to your advantage. 



 Organizations like the Illinois Community Health Workers Association (ILCHWA) are doing great work connecting community members with resources. We are all about making sure community health workers are at the center of decisions affecting their work. We can learn a lot from their approach. 



 #1. Building Strong Partnerships 



 Think of your community as a network. It’s bustling with people and organizations, each with unique strengths. Building strong partnerships is about connecting those strengths . It’s about working together to achieve more than you could alone. It’s not just about who you know, but who you work with. 



 Why are partnerships so important? 



 
 They expand your reach. 



 They bring in new resources. 



 They build trust within the community. 
 



 A good partnership is a win-win . Each partner brings something valuable to the table. This shared value creates a stronger impact . 



 How do you build these rock-solid partnerships? 



 
 Identify potential partners. 
 
 Who shares your goals? 



 Who works with the same community? 



 Look for organizations with complementary services . A local food bank might partner well with a health clinic. They both serve the same people, but in different ways . This creates a powerful synergy. 
 
 



 Reach out and start a conversation. 
 
 Don’t just send a generic email. 



 Make it personal. 



 Show that you understand their work. 



 Explain how a partnership could benefit both organizations. 



 Be clear about what you bring to the table. 



 Pro Tip: Start small. A joint event or a cross-promotion can be a great way to test the waters . It’s a low-risk way to see if a long-term partnership makes sense.

 Keep the lines open. 



 Share updates.
